description.narrative: Kuwait Energy (the Company or Kuwait Energy) is an oil and gas exploration and development (E&P) company focused on the MENA region. The proposed investment by IFC will fund (i) the partial refinancing of the Companys existing debt; (ii) continuation of existing exploration, development and production activities in Egypt, Ukraine and, potentially, Russia; (iii) general corporate purposes; and (iv) capital expenditures in other jurisdictions as expressly approved by IFC.

The Project will lead to further exploration, appraisal and development of domestic oil and gas resources in Egypt, Ukraine and Russia, helping meet domestic demand and slow the pace of decline in oil production in Egypt as well as support Ukraine''s gas production and help reduce the country''s dependency on imports. (i) Contribution to Government Revenues: The financing provided to KEC will be used to fund activities that are expected to result in higher and longer production, positively impacting the revenues that host governments receive through production sharing, royalties, corporate taxes as well as other methods. (ii) Local and regional spending: The Project is expected to contribute to local and regional spending as part of the field services and operational supplies will be procured domestically. (iii) Employment: The Project will create new jobs. KEC''s direct local employment in the MENA Region, Ukraine and Russia is expected to increase as the company further develops its assets. Even though the Project''s impact on employment is expected to be marginal compared to the unemployment situation in the MENA Region, this may potentially increase given the early stage nature of some of the target assets.

name.narrative: In Egypt, Kuwait Energy has interests in three onshore producing assets (Area A in Gulf of Suez, and East Ras Qattara and Burg El Arab concessions, both in the Western Desert), one development asset (Abu Sennan in the Western Desert) and an early exploration asset (Block 6 in Southern Egypt). Kuwait Energy is the operator in Area A, Burg El Arab and Abu Sennan. In Ukraine, Kuwait Energy has a 100% participating interest in two onshore licenses of which one is a producing asset: Bilousivski-Chornukhi (producing asset) and North Yablunivska (non producing development asset). Kuwait Energy is the operator of all the Ukrainian assets. In Russia, Kuwait Energy has interests in two onshore licenses: Luzskoye (a producing asset with exploration potential) and Chikshina (an exploration asset). Kuwait Energy is the operator in both assets. Governance Risks Assessment: IFC has reviewed project benefits and associated governance risks and believes that the project should be supported. In coming to this view, IFC considered the magnitude of fiscal benefits, governance metrics and the World Banks engagement to support good governance. The oil and gas sector in Egypt has historically been stable, and the issuing of licenses and the sharing mechanism for revenue, taxation and royalty between private companies and the public sector can be considered relatively transparent. There are governance and transparency challenges in both Russia and Ukraine, and the oil and gas sectors in both countries have occasionally been subject to annulments of licenses; however, given the size of the Ukrainian and Russian assets relative to Kuwait Energys total reserves in terms of value as well as Kuwait Energys stable track record in Ukraine and Russia, IFC believes that the risks are mitigated and acceptable. Moreover, as per IFC requirements, the Company will publicly disclose all material payments made to the governments.
